blocks.raw:
<Callout>
Mesopotamian architecture tests your ability to identify structural innovations, building types, and the relationship between religion and urban planning in civilization's earliest complex society. The LEA expects knowledge of ziggurats, palaces, city walls, and the architectural responses to a floodplain environment.
</Callout>

blocks.raw:
<Tip>
**Memory Aid: Ziggurat Symbolism.** Think of the ziggurat as a staircase to heaven—literally stepping upward from earth toward the divine. Each level is higher, each is smaller, each represents spiritual ascension. The temple shrine at the apex is where gods and humans supposedly met.
</Tip>

blocks.raw:
<Note>
**Key Clarification:** Do not confuse ziggurat with pyramid. Ziggurats are stepped structures serving temples and ritual functions. Pyramids are Egyptian tombs built with stone blocks and smooth sides. While both are monumental, their materials, purposes, and forms differ fundamentally.
</Note>

blocks.raw:
<Warn>
**Critical Distinction:** Do not overstate knowledge of internal layout. Ziggurats and palaces have sparse interior documentation. Avoid inventing detailed room descriptions. What we know comes from excavation and textual hints; acknowledge this limitation when discussing Mesopotamian architecture.
</Warn>

blocks.raw: <WikiExamTable headers={["Structure", "Location", "Date", "Builder/Period", "Key Feature"]} rows={[["**Ziggurat of Ur**", "Ur (modern Iraq)", "c. 2100 BCE", "Ur-Nammu (Ur III)", "Three stepped platforms, dimensions 210 × 150 feet (64 × 46 m), height originally 70-100 feet (21-30 m), mud brick"], ["**Palace of Hammurabi**", "Babylon", "1792–1750 BCE", "Hammurabi (Old Babylon)", "Courtyard plan typical of Babylonian palaces; exact palace layout unknown due to high water table preventing excavation"], ["**Palace of Sennacherib**", "Nineveh (Assyrian)", "705–681 BCE", "Sennacherib", "Monumental gateways guarded by lamassu (ten total colossal figures, weighing up to 30 tons each), extensive relief programs, mud brick and stone"], ["**Walls of Uruk**", "Uruk", "c. 3100–2900 BCE", "Early Dynastic period (Gilgamesh c. 2900-2350 BCE)", "Mud brick walls with baked-brick reinforcement, 9 kilometers in circumference, defensive and flood-control function"], ["**Temple of Marduk (Etemenanki Ziggurat)**", "Babylon", "Construction phases unclear; Nebuchadnezzar II rebuilt/completed c. 605-562 BCE", "Nabopolassar and Nebuchadnezzar II", "Seven-stepped ziggurat, roughly 91 meters high and 91 meters square base, temple shrine on apex; Hanging Gardens (archaeologically unverified)"], ["**Nippur Temple Precinct**", "Nippur", "c. 2000–1800 BCE", "Multiple builders across periods", "Ziggurat of Enlil dedicated to the sky god Enlil, temple complexes, religious and administrative center"]]} />
